subject.title: Session Routing Bugs: CLI routing to wrong session, WeChat ID inconsistency, and session deadlock from message flooding

question: How should maintainers split ownership for #88204 across core sessions_send/TUI routing, WeChat plugin routing, background-event isolation, and meaningful-activity sorting?
rationale: Current source proves some core routing gaps, but the issue bundles multiple owner boundaries and two already-open canonical subproblems, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent split or product semantics.

options.title: Split into canonical tracks
options.body: Keep #88204 open only as an umbrella until #93255, #51028, and new WeChat/background-event repro tracks each have an owner and validation path.

options.title: Sponsor one broad core project
options.body: Treat the issue as a larger session-routing reliability project that redesigns channel identity, activity timestamps, and internal-event isolation together.

options.title: Defer plugin-specific pieces
options.body: Track only the core #93255 and #51028 work now, and require a fresh WeChat plugin repro before any core/plugin boundary change for the remaining claims.

recommendation.title: Split into canonical tracks
recommendation.body: Keep #88204 open only as an umbrella until #93255, #51028, and new WeChat/background-event repro tracks each have an owner and validation path.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the broadest recent history across the implicated sessions_send, gateway sessions, and TUI files, making him the best routing owner for the split decision.
